title: Sakralraum im säkularen Kontext
summary: The Paulinum – St Paul’s University Hall and University Church in Leipzig – was opened in 2017 as a hybrid space. It serves simultaneously as the university’s ceremonial hall, the university church, a venue for exhibitions of traditional church furnishings organised by the Custody, and a concert hall for the University Music Department; it was specifically planned and designed to accommodate these diverse uses and spatial interpretations. What insights can be gained from its use to date regarding the search for sacred spaces in the interplay between the church and other spheres of society? The contributions in this book offer an initial assessment of synergies and areas of tension, mutual harmonies and interconnections in its use; they shed light on the Paulinum as a place of cultural memory and as a potential city church; they look back at historical hybridity in the space; and they open up comparative perspectives on religious spaces at universities, church reconstruction projects in eastern Germany, museums in churches, university churches in other locations, and the spatial divisions being introduced into church interiors. In doing so, the volume as a whole contributes to the exploration of the potential for the transformation of sacred spaces through cooperation between religious and secular actors. This volume brings together interdisciplinary perspectives from Protestant and Catholic theology, history and art history, sociology and ethnology, and the study of religion, alongside insights into people’s experiences of using the Paulinum.
